title: Void Ending in a Conjunction with Venus
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The conjunction is the closest bond the Moon makes: at it, her strength takes on the nature of the planet she has joined, and the doctrine of the fifth quality treats her meeting with the Sun as the strongest of all her figures. A course that closes on a conjunction ends in union rather than separation, the Moon's virtue soaked through with the planet's own nature.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a conjunction with Venus, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of her sweetness and her song. Venus governs taste, the text says, and with it beauty and love: poetic meter, songs, dancing, painting, and perfumes fall to her, with places of music and merriment among her locations. She is the Lesser Fortune, and her benevolence fits the works of youths, pleasures, and women. Pearls are her stones, the sweet smells are hers, and her colors are sky blue and gold fading into green.
